name: Familial Clubfoot Due to 17q23.1q23.2 Microduplication
aliases: Hereditary Talipes Equinovarus Associated with 17q23.1q23.2 Microduplication
Familial Congenital Talipes Equinovarus with 17q23 Duplication

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Genetic Diagnosis of Familial Clubfoot due to 17q23.1q23.2 Microduplication

criteria.description: Presence of congenital talipes equinovarus (clubfoot) deformity
Positive family history of clubfoot consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Identification of 17q23.1q23.2 microduplication by chromosomal microarray or other molecular genetic testing
Exclusion of other syndromic causes of clubfoot

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of congenital clubfoot with positive family history and confirmed 17q23.1q23.2 microduplication
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies on clinical presentation combined with molecular genetic confirmation.

imaging: Radiographs showing talipes equinovarus deformity with hindfoot varus and forefoot adduction
Ultrasound or MRI may show calf muscle hypoplasia
other: Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance pattern

distinguishingFeatures: Usually sporadic cases without family history
Neuromuscular involvement and more severe limb deformities

redFlags: Progressive worsening of foot deformity despite treatment
Presence of neurological deficits in lower limbs
Signs of syndromic involvement or multiple congenital anomalies
references: Orphanet: Familial clubfoot due to 17q23.1q23.2 microduplication, ORPHA:238578
Recent molecular studies on 17q23.1q23.2 microduplication and clubfoot phenotype
